title: Effects of hiking downhill using trekking poles while carrying external loads
claims: Fifteen experienced male hikers were tested with and without poles across three pack conditions: no pack, day pack at 15% body weight, and large expedition pack at 30% body weight.
Pole use significantly reduced the sagittal-plane moment at each lower extremity joint and reduced peak power absorption at the ankle and knee.
These reductions held across pack conditions; the pack only produced larger power generation at the hip.
The authors conclude reduced forces, moments and power around the joints help lower loading on the lower extremity; the study was downhill hiking in experienced males, not trail running.
